searchText: <@!364458974906548225> (and maybe <@456226577798135808>) On your recent call with PegaSys' Team X you mentioned that the merry-go-round sync would be maybe 15-20 MBytes in 15seconds for a 24-hour sync. That would mean 1-1.3 MByte/s or roughly 10Mbps. That would would be difficult for many people to sustain on their networks, especially once one adds in protocol overheads and possibly encryption. Is your answer for those on slow networks to simply use a slower merry-go-round? <@!364458974906548225> Also, 15-20MBytes/15 sec == only 84-115 GB/day. Is that enough for a full sync? I understand full state is larger than that... <@!692550965856829481> I gave this number as an example, to let you imagine what it might be like. I did not test whether this is going to work on not The state is not larger than 84-115 Gb. Again, we need to see how large it is if we count in the proofs, but i would expect something like 60 Gb perhaps > Since the Sync call will be at 2am in Brisbane 😴 , could the meeting please be recorded so that we can listen to it in the morning? <@!688889240125308981> I'll also do another machine-translation and digest of the call if that's helpful (I'm also in Asia time, although not *quite* as far east as you) Call in 25 hours <@!692550965856829481> here is a document that attempts to specify a protocol that satisfies the desired criteria. Maybe reading that will shed some light on the broader concept. https://notes.ethereum.org/n2bIgRe5SReOM7BZle4jaQ This is by no means a complete protocol but just an attempt to take a stab at defining something as a starting point. I know others (alexey) have fundamentally different approaches they are looking into.
